findings.title: The `http:`/`https:` scheme guard in parseAllowlistEntry is asserted by no test — all four fixtures are caught by the PATH guard instead
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Confirmed non-equivalent by inspection. All four fixtures have a non-empty, non-'/' pathname (file:///etc/passwd -> '/etc/passwd', data:text/html,<script> -> 'text/html,<script>', blob:https://admin.example/1234 -> 'https://admin.example/1234', javascript:alert(1) -> 'alert(1)'), so with the scheme throw deleted every one still throws AdminOriginConfigError from the path throw two guards later. The mutant is observably different: readAdminAppOrigins() returns ['ftp://admin.example'] / ['null'] instead of throwing for entries whose pathname is '/' (ftp://, ws://, wss://, file://host) — that is an exported-function behaviour change, so 'equivalent' cannot be claimed. Not an unexecuted branch: the test DOES run the scheme guard, its assertion simply cannot distinguish which guard fired. Security impact is nil today because normalizeOrigin independently enforces http(s) on the request side, so no extra origin becomes admissible; the defect is in the ORACLE. One-line fix: add an entry whose ONLY disqualifier is the scheme (e.g. 'ftp://admin.example' or 'ws://admin.example') to the fixture list.

findings.title: The Edge-safety guard's `node:` entry can never match, and side-effect imports are invisible — both node-builtin import shapes survive
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Confirmed non-equivalent and semantically meaningful. The membership test is `s === bad || s.startsWith(`${bad}/`)`; for bad='node:' that demands the specifier be exactly 'node:' or start with 'node:/', neither of which is a real specifier, so 'node:crypto' passes (M27 survived). Separately the extractor is /from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g, so a bare `import 'node:crypto';` yields no specifier at all (M28 survived). The 'node builtins' third of the test's stated property is enforced by nothing, which is the exact hole the cited precedent (src/lib/auth/__tests__/admin-transport.test.ts:114-119) documents a prior red-team pass walking through twice. The '@/lib/db', 'postgres', 'bullmq', 'openai', '@anthropic-ai/sdk', '@supabase/supabase-js' and 'ioredis' entries DO match and are unaffected. No live defect: the graph carries no node: import at HEAD. Fix: special-case the scheme (s.startsWith('node:')) and widen the extractor to /(?:from|import)\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g.

findings.title: `ADR 0026 D14` is cited for the normalized-echo rule, but ADR 0026 contains only D1-D8 and no canonical-output decision at all
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Re-resolved against 4f132aae: `rg -o '\bD[0-9]{1,2}\b' docs/adr/0026-admin-api-cors.md` yields D1 D2 D3 D4 D5 D6 D7 D8 only, and `rg -i 'canonical|normaliz'` over the same ADR returns zero hits. The other citations in the diff DO resolve: ADR 0026 D1/D2/D3/D4/D7 exist, and both verbatim quotes check out (D2 'Loopback is a separate code rule, not a list entry' at 0026:114; D4 'One predicate owns the origin comparison' at 0026:179). findings.title: The terminal AdminOriginConfigError edge-throw (500 on every /api/admin/** request) has no rule row in the alerting runbook
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The diff adds an operator-actionable TERMINAL path: a malformed ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS makes readAdminAppOrigins() throw inside the Edge proxy on every /api/admin/** request. The emitting half exists (src/instrumentation.ts:69-77 initialises Sentry for NEXT_RUNTIME==='edge', and onRequestError=Sentry.captureRequestError is exported), but docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md has no rule row for it: `rg -i 'proxy|middleware|CORS|origin|ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS'` over that runbook returns one unrelated hit (line 882). Duty 5 emits P1 when either half is missing; this is 'an emitted signal with no rule row'. Mitigants for the arbiter: (a) the path is unreachable in every environment today because ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS is unset everywhere and unset parses to [] without throwing; (b) .claude/reference/env-vars.md documents the failure and the redeploy remedy, so the destination-action half is written down, just not as a Sentry rule.
